security_audit.summary: Most static matches are Markdown formatting, documentation URLs, or scoped product-status checks and are false positives. Confirmed findings show that local workflow files and CLI action output can influence agent behavior without integrity or trust boundaries. Automatic installer handling also lacks authenticated provenance.

remediation.issue: Local workflow files are loaded and followed without trust boundaries.
remediation.suggestion: Treat ~/.onchainos workflow files as untrusted data. Require signed or packaged workflows, validate a strict schema, and never execute embedded commands automatically.

remediation.issue: CLI action output influences workflow control.
remediation.suggestion: Parse CLI output as structured data and allow only documented action values. Reject unexpected values and display them as data.

remediation.issue: Missing CLI may trigger automatic installation without authenticated provenance.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation and verify a signed release against a pinned public key from an official source.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Local Workflow Is Followed As Instructions
semantic_findings.description: The daily-brief flow directs the agent to load and follow a local workflow file. A user-writable local file can inject instructions into later agent actions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited text explicitly requires loading and following local workflow content, with no validation or untrusted-content boundary.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted CLI Output May Control Flow
semantic_findings.description: Preflight treats a CLI action value as an instruction for subsequent agent behavior. Compromised or malformed CLI output could influence the workflow.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The preflight flow uses action-oriented CLI output to select behavior, but the document does not specify schema validation or an allowlist.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Installer Trust Is Not Authenticated
semantic_findings.description: The preflight flow permits automatic installation when the CLI is missing. Downloading an installer and checksum from the same unspecified source does not establish authenticity.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Automatic installation expands impact, and checksum verification alone cannot protect against a source that serves both altered binary and checksum.

content.user_title: Guide users through OKX Onchain OS onboarding
content.value_statement: New users can struggle to find correct Onchain OS, OKX.AI, and support paths. This skill classifies questions and routes users to documented onboarding guidance.
actual_capabilities: Classifies first-time Onchain OS and getting-started questions.
Explains supported onboarding and product-introduction paths.
Routes OKX.AI questions to role-registration guidance.
Routes support, complaint, feedback, and bug-report intents.
Avoids direct swaps, wallet actions, balances, and token operations.
limitations: Does not execute on-chain transactions or manage wallets.
Does not provide investment, legal, or financial advice.
Depends on referenced OKX documentation remaining available.
Does not replace official customer support for account-specific issues.

use_cases.title: Onboard a first-time user
use_cases.description: Explain what Onchain OS offers and select a safe getting-started path.

use_cases.title: Understand OKX.AI roles
use_cases.description: Route questions about User, ASP, or Evaluator registration to correct guidance.

use_cases.title: Find support channel
use_cases.description: Direct complaints, feedback, and bug reports to appropriate support guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Start onboarding
prompt_templates.prompt: I am new to Onchain OS. What can I do, and how should I start?

prompt_templates.title: Learn OKX.AI
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain OKX.AI and help me understand available roles.

prompt_templates.title: Choose registration path
prompt_templates.prompt: I want to join OKX.AI as an Evaluator. What guidance should I read first?

prompt_templates.title: Route support issue
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to report a bug. Which support path fits this request?

output: Clear boundary for direct on-chain actions

output_examples.input: I need help with an OKX.AI role.
output: Reminder to use official account support for account issues

best_practices: State goal and whether you are new, registered, or seeking support.
Use official links for account, credential, and registration actions.
Keep private keys, secret keys, and passphrases out of prompts.
anti_patterns: Do not ask this guide to swap tokens or operate a wallet.
Do not share API keys, secret keys, passphrases, or recovery phrases.
Do not treat routing guidance as financial or legal advice.

faq.question: Does this skill perform token swaps?
faq.answer: No. It only routes onboarding, product, and support questions.

faq.question: Can it access my wallet?
faq.answer: No. It does not perform wallet or token operations.

faq.question: Can it explain OKX.AI?
faq.answer: Yes. It routes OKX.AI introductions and role-registration questions.

faq.question: Can it file a support request for me?
faq.answer: It can identify support guidance, but it does not replace official support channels.

faq.question: Should I share API credentials?
faq.answer: No. Never provide API keys, secret keys, passphrases, or recovery phrases.

faq.question: Does it give investment advice?
faq.answer: No. It provides product guidance and does not offer financial advice.
